editorial.purpose_and_first_use: The plain first-use lesson explains requesting a specific Financial Analysis task, providing dated balances, reviewing classification choices, running the calculation and reading its result and detail. It introduces the wider workflow without pretending this net-debt example teaches all eight registered engines.
editorial.inputs_and_request: Read this localized context and both four-row source statements. February contains a 65,000 EUR loan, 27,000 available cash, 5,000 restricted deposit and 52,000 ordinary trade payables. The authored request defines loan less available cash and excludes the other two items. It explicitly limits coverage and does not prefill professional approval or ask the learner to write technical contracts.
editorial.execution_and_checkpoints: The test imports the actual source, records its exact hash and the test-only interpretation of the requested definition in current case contracts, then runs the registered net-debt engine and normal contract audit. The lesson checkpoints ask what is measured and why a balance is included or excluded. No model arithmetic or generated calculation code substitutes for the native result.
editorial.deliverable_and_next_action: The actual prepared metrics and four line items support a concise localized Codex delivery note with separate included-result and excluded-item tables. The note links the native result, detailed rows and contract audit. This is the ordinary delivery stage described by the skill, exercised with authored test prose, rather than a new engine-generated report. It explains the supplied definition and the need to check source completeness and conclusions. Source tie-out remains not_assessed and report_ready remains false.
editorial.practice_and_repeat: March runs independently at 31 March with the same definition and new balances: loan 66,000, available cash 35,000, restricted deposit 5,000 and trade payables 53,000 EUR. Native net debt is 31,000 EUR. The learner compares dates and balances with the preserved February result and repeats by describing a financial question and reviewing the proposed analysis and assumptions.
editorial.language_and_pacing: Read the it outline, context and delivery wording. The JSON calculation contract retains canonical English field names; the explanation and result tables use the selected working language. Six stages total 390 seconds, with time for processing and questions allowed to extend the lesson. Native learner and voice behavior are not attested.
